$comment: D-CSUBSET-GNU-ATTRIBUTE (TF-C72/C73): the `packed`/`aligned` COMPOSITE and UNION-MEMBER shapes the real macOS SDK headers use, gated on `sizeof`, `_Alignof` and a runtime ADDRESS. COMPLEMENT of `examples/c-subset/gnu_aligned_attribute/`, not a duplicate: that example owns the POSITION axis for a lone `aligned(N)`; this one owns (a) `packed` COMBINED with `aligned` in one clause, where a sink that honors one and drops the other makes a layout no single-attribute example can distinguish, (b) `packed` ALONE, whose observable is a SHRUNK struct (5/1) — the opposite direction from every `aligned` row, (c) the UNION member slot (`unionField`, a different config row from `structField`) which had no runtime witness, and (d) `_Alignof` as an observable, the one surface that sees a raised alignment on a composite whose SIZE did not change. CLANG GROUND TRUTH, measured not assumed: `struct S { char a; int b; } __attribute__((packed, aligned(16)))` is sizeof 16 / _Alignof 16 (NOT 5/16 — the raised alignment pads the packed 5 bytes back out); packed-only is 5/1; `typedef unsigned long long T __attribute__((aligned(8)))` is 8/8. DSS agrees on every one. ★★ NON-VACUITY PROVEN PER CHECK: each of the 9 checks was isolated into its OWN single-check program carrying the EXACT shipped declaration block, and built twice — as written, and with exactly the attribute that check depends on deleted. Every check goes 42 -> its own exit number, in DSS and in clang alike: 1 sizeof(PA)==16 -> 1, 2 _Alignof(PA)==16 -> 2, 3 &pa%16 -> 3, 4 sizeof(PK)==5 -> 4, 5 _Alignof(PK)==1 -> 5, 6 offset PK.b==1 -> 6, 7 sizeof(UM)==32 -> 7, 8 _Alignof(UM)==32 -> 8, 9 &um.m%32 -> 9. Two extra columns were measured for rows 1/2/3: dropping ONLY `packed` moves them (1/2/3) and dropping ONLY `aligned(16)` does NOT (42) — correct, and precisely why rows 4/5/6 exist on a packed-ONLY struct, which is the shape where losing `packed` is observable. ★ THE TYPEDEF ROW CARRIES NO CHECK, DELIBERATELY: `sdk_u64` is declared, defined and RETURNED so the literal SDK spelling is exercised end to end, but nothing gates on it — `aligned(8)` on `unsigned long long` asks for exactly the alignment the aliasee already has, and MEASURED, deleting the attribute still exits 42. Vacuous by construction, not by placement. DSS's observable behavior for a typedef asking for MORE is compile-time and fail-loud (`typedef int T __attribute__((aligned(16)));` -> error[S002F] 'on a typedef cannot be honored: the alias resolves to the same type as its aliasee, whose alignment is 4'), which no running binary can witness and which DIVERGES from clang (clang accepts it and reports _Alignof 16) — that divergence belongs in a unit pin, not in a green corpus example. ★★ THE OFFSET BREAKERS (`data_pad_a`, `data_pad_b`, `bss_pad_c`) ARE LOAD-BEARING; do not delete them and do not add an over-aligned global without one. The first over-aligned object in a section lands at the page-aligned section START, so an address check on it holds whether or not the sink ran — that exact vacuity was measured in a sibling example and cost three of its five checks. Each breaker is one byte of the SAME section class as the object it precedes (.data ahead of the initialized `pa`/`pk`, .bss ahead of the uninitialized `um`). The `release` arm is MANDATORY, not decoration: the point is witnessing that the real SHIPPED optimizer PRESERVES the layout rather than re-laying-out the globals. VERIFIED clang-clean (`-fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra -isysroot $(xcrun --show-sdk-path)`: zero errors, zero warnings) and the clang-built binary independently exits 42, so the expected exit code is ground truth from a real toolchain — a corpus example must witness REAL C, not merely C that DSS happens to accept.
